assessment: The stipulated observations support difficulty entering conversations and identifying preparation, but establish neither proficiency mismatch nor the causes of lost practice. Useful speaking time and coordination savings remain unverified. Two bounded paper-based capabilities could be tested within ordinary sessions.

openings.claim: A speculative self-adjusting conversation sheet could let partners begin a useful exchange without shared attendance history or public proficiency labels. It would combine a fresh shared scenario, optional sentence supports and extension prompts, and alternating speaker turns.
openings.delta: Dependencies are understandable support choices, prompts that work independently of prior sessions, partners accepting different supports, and balanced turns that still feel useful. The presently testable partial capability is a printed scenario with optional supports; participants select or change supports without declaring a level.
openings.prediction: If missing shared context constrains entry, fresh scenarios should shorten first-exchange latency. If support mismatch matters separately, optional supports should increase useful speaking reports even with fresh scenarios held constant.
openings.probe: Within existing practice time, counterbalance short rounds using fresh versus familiar scenarios and optional versus existing supports. Observe first-exchange latency and individual speaking minutes; collect anonymous usefulness reports. Keep the familiar opening ritual. Across six sessions, count all attendances in the 80% reporting target and log total volunteer minutes against the under-90-minute limit, including preparation of variants.
assumptions: Participants can use support options without public proficiency labels.
Observation and printing fit existing volunteer capacity; this must be measured.
Timed speech alone does not establish usefulness.

openings.claim: Would a conspicuously dated paper preparation panel prevent obsolete-task selection, or do participants need clearer task wording even when viewing the correct sheet?
openings.delta: A future paper system that always exposes the current task depends on version recognition, comprehensible wording and a route for missed-session arrivals. Test version recognition first rather than assuming messaging access is the cause.
openings.prediction: If version confusion dominates, date emphasis should reduce earlier-task answers. Persisting errors while the correct panel is visible would implicate comprehension or attention instead.
openings.probe: Compare ordinary and date-emphasized printed panels with identical task wording; ask participants to identify the next task with papers visible and again at exit. Give missed-session arrivals the current panel and allow participation without preparation. Track the 85% identification target and printing time.
assumptions: Printed panels remain available at every session.
Date recognition is accessible to participants; neither smartphones nor accounts are required.
